text: Install a fix. You have {n} fix points.
There is no clock. If three visitors leave without help, the health center closes for the day. You can also finish the run yourself.
The assisted counter is a person, so it always helps, but it is slower: it fits a person with no smartphone best, and only so many people can wait there.
Each visitor tries the same task: book a check-up and get a queue number. You see the kiosk the way they do, and every filter is also written out in words.
When they get stuck, spend fix points on fixes: large text, voice guide, captions, language choice, a lower screen or an assisted counter. Then try again.

Each visitor brings 2 fix points (you can keep up to 5). Fixes stay installed, so later visitors get easier. Points come from satisfaction stars, fixes that were ready in advance, and fixes that help several people.
The blur and other filters only ever change the pretend kiosk. The game buttons stay clear and easy to use.

Run the health-center kiosk for as long as you can. Visitors keep coming, each with different needs. Try the kiosk as them, then install fixes until they are served. Fixes stay installed, but new visitors bring new needs. The run ends when three people have left.

The health center has a new kiosk, and not everyone can use it. Five visitors will come. See the kiosk through their eyes, then spend fix points to make it work for them. A person who leaves is a lesson, not a fail: you always finish.
